props.gloss_en: those on a mitzvah errand are exempt from the sukkah
'when you sit in your house' -- to the exclusion of one engaged in a mitzva
'and when you walk on the way' -- to the exclusion of a groom
from here they said: one who marries a virgin is exempt [from the Shema]
and one who marries a widow is obligated
Rav Huna: [the verse's 'when you walk on the way' is read] like 'the way'
as the way is voluntary, so too all [the obligation is in] the voluntary
to the exclusion of this one, who is engaged in a mitzva
if so, let the verse say 'when sitting and when walking'; what is 'when YOU sit / when YOU walk'? in your own walking you are obligated; in walking of a mitzva you are exempt
one who marries a virgin is preoccupied; one who marries a widow is not
Rav: a mourner is obligated in all the mitzvot stated in the Torah
except tefillin [from which the mourner is exempt]
for 'splendour' is stated of them
here he is preoccupied with the preoccupation of a mitzva; there, with the preoccupation of the voluntary
one who is engaged in a mitzva is exempt from [another] mitzva
is it derived from here? it is derived from there: 'and there were men who were impure by the corpse of a person' (Bamidbar 9:6)
who were those men? they were the bearers of Joseph's coffin
they were Mishael and Eltzafan, who were occupied with Nadav and Avihu
if they were the bearers of Joseph's coffin, they could already have become pure; if Mishael and Eltzafan, they could have become pure
rather, they were occupied with a met mitzva, and their seventh day fell on the eve of Pesach
as it is said 'and they could not perform the Pesach on that day' -- on that day they could not, but on the next day they could
had it taught there alone: [they were exempt] because the time of the Pesach obligation had not arrived; but here, where the time of the Shema has arrived, say not
had it taught here alone: because there is no karet; but there, where there is karet, say not
since the Merciful One said to Ezekiel 'bind your splendour upon you' (Yechezkel 24:17) -- you are obligated, but everyone else is exempt
and this [exemption] applies on the first day
as it is written 'and its end as a bitter day' (Amos 8:10)
Rav: a mourner is obligated in the sukkah
Rav: one who suffers [in the sukkah] is exempt from the sukkah
that applies to suffering that comes of itself
but here he is the one paining himself; he ought to settle his mind
Rav: the groom, the groomsmen and all the wedding party are exempt from the sukkah all seven days
what is the reason? because they need to rejoice
there is no rejoicing except in the chupa
there is no rejoicing except in the place of the meal
Abaye: [the chupa is not made in the sukkah] because of seclusion
Rava: because of the groom's distress
what is between them? where people commonly go in and out there
for the one who says 'because of seclusion' -- there is no [concern]
for the one who says 'because of the groom's distress' -- there is [the concern]
R' Zeira: I ate in the sukkah and rejoiced in the chupa
and all the more did my heart rejoice, that I was doing two
the groom, the groomsmen and all the wedding party are exempt from prayer and from tefillin
and they [the groom included] are obligated in the reading of the Shema
in R' Sheila's name they said: the groom is exempt [from the Shema]
and the groomsmen and all the wedding party are obligated

scribes of [Torah] scrolls, tefillin and mezuzot, they, their merchants and their merchants' merchants, and all who are engaged in the work of Heaven, are exempt from the Shema, from prayer, from tefillin and from all the mitzvot stated in the Torah
[all who are engaged in the work of Heaven] -- to include sellers of techelet
travellers by day are exempt from the sukkah by day
and obligated at night
travellers by night are exempt from the sukkah at night
and obligated by day
travellers by day and by night are exempt from the sukkah both by day and by night
those going for a matter of mitzva are exempt both by day and by night
as Rav Chisda and Rabba bar Rav Huna, when they went to the Exilarch's house on the Shabbat of the festival, slept on the bank of the Sura
they said: we are on a mitzvah errand, and exempt
city guards by day are exempt from the sukkah by day
and obligated at night
city guards by night are exempt from the sukkah at night
and obligated by day
city guards by day and by night are exempt from the sukkah both by day and by night
guards of gardens and orchards are exempt both by day and by night
Abaye: 'you shall dwell' (Vayikra 23:42) -- in the manner that you reside
Rava: a breach calls to the thief
what is between them? where he guards a pile of fruit
